chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hakim al-Hannat, from Durays, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Permission (to fight) has been given to those who are fought against because they have been oppressed, and indeed Allah is competent to support them.'
He said: 'It is Ali, al- Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them).'
ai.seo_question: Who is the verse 'Permission (to fight) has been given to those who are fought against' revealed about in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) interpreting the verse 'Permission (to fight) has been given to those who are fought against...' (22:39) as specifically referring to the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby establishing their martyrdom and struggle as the primary context for this verse. This exegesis elevates the status of Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (a.s.) not merely as recipients of divine aid but as the archetypal oppressed who were granted the right to defend themselves against injustice. This interpretation underscores the theological significance of their suffering and avenging their blood within Shia eschatology and jurisprudence.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Abbās ibn Ma’rūf, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥakam Al-Ḥannāť, from Ďurays, from Abī Khālid Al-Kābuli, who said:

I heard Abā Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) explain the verse, “Permission (to fight) is given to those against whom war is made, because they have been oppressed, and verily Allāh is potent to help them” [22:39].
(The Imam (a.s.) said), “This verse was revealed about ‘Ali, Ḥasan, and Ḥusain (a.s.).”
